title: Residual of the ISS-T036CAL-011 fix: an unknown cancelled event that carries NO start time (id only) still holds every UNLINKED Gmail row as unproven-calendar-history, in both scopes, until the state is reset
evidence: Pinned by the test 'RESIDUAL (ISS-TOMBSTONE-001)': calendar [c0, c1 (linked to g1)] + Gmail [g1, g5, g6] + tombstone {id:'ghost',cancelled:true} -> calendarEvents [c0,c1], candidates [g1]; g5 and g6 (no calendar twin) are held. Reach: ONLY Gmail rows with no calendar twin on record (e.g. email-only webinar registrations); never a calendar row, never a Gmail row linked to one, never newStartsBlocked. The hold persists with the stored tombstone row (no expiry; ends with a state reset). An outsider can only trigger it if Google returns the cancelled invite as an id-only resource; with a start (the usual shape for a cancelled invite) only Gmail rows at that exact start (or that exact conference identity) are held.
fix_direction: A bare id cannot be tied to any Gmail row, and holding is the only way to keep 'do not join a meeting cancelled before it was ever stored'. Options for the Approver (Umesh): accept; or add an expiry (needs the first-seen tick stored on the tombstone row, a state-shape change); or drop the hold for id-only tombstones (accepts joining a cancelled meeting through its Gmail copy).
